# BMS / DJMax Keysound Slicer UX Audit

**Research note.** This is an evidence audit, not a claim that every requested tool has a public specification. I found a maintained Sayaslicer README/issues set, legacy Woslicer/BMHelper guides, a Mid2BMS/FL workflow, and the key-sound reference pages. I did **not** find a public Woslicer III issue tracker or enough primary user comments to support “top 10 Woslicer issues”; those gaps are marked rather than invented. “P0/P1/P2” below is my product severity assessment, not a label used by the cited projects.

## 1. Comparison table

| Tool | Workflow evidenced | Top 3 pain points / limits | Max slices / snap | Export method |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Sayaslicer** | Load audio; place/import markers; optionally apply offset, arbitrary snap, zero-cross/tail removal/fade; save project; copy BMSE or iBMSC clipboard; export keysounds and/or keysound list. It can import MIDI markers and a Mid2BMS renamer array. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) | (1) iBMSC arbitrary-resolution markers can make a BMS save fail or lose keysounds/gamemode; fallback is BMSE clipboard, which rounds to 192nd. (2) Very large files once lagged/failed above 2 GB/sample-count threshold (issue says fixed). (3) Planned BPM-change support is still described as incomplete. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) · [Issue #5](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/5) | No slice-count maximum published. Snap is **1/1–1/192**; BMSE path rounds to nearest 192nd. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) | `M` exports slices; `K` copies a keysound list; `Shift+K` appends a BMS in the audio folder; `V`/`Shift+V` copy BMSE/iBMSC placement data. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) |
| **Woslicer II** | Drag WAV/OGG; set BPM/step division; place points; optionally load BMHelper clipboard positions; set starting sound number; copy BMSE clipboard; `M` exports numbered audio. [BMS Creation Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7MuFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit) · [guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) | Manual multi-application “ceremony”: DAW/MIDI → BMHelper → Woslicer → BMSE/text editor. 32-bit-float preview is unsupported; old base-16/hex mode must normally stay off; tails need manual adjustment. [BMS Creation Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7MuFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit) · [guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) | No maximum published in the sources. Snap is to BPM and step divisions; exact denominator range not documented in the fetched guide. | `M` writes many WAVs; `V` emits BMSE clipboard object data; `.wos` saves progress. [BMS Creation Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7MuFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit) |
| **Woslicer III** | Open WAV/OGG; enter BPM; adjust offset/amplification; divide by cursor; “総出力”/export all; place the resulting files and clipboard sequence in BMSE. [BMS Creation Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7MuFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit) · [ぷるれこ guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) | A guide explicitly recommends II because III generates clicks at the beginning of each sliced sound. A technical investigation attributes a pop to reverse/reflect tail handling and a one-sample zero insertion. Cursor workflow is less keyboard-efficient than II. [BMS Creation Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7MuFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit) · [Qiita investigation](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/79db943d2e3447adee71) | No maximum or exact denominator range found. BPM/step slicing is documented; offset/amplification are exposed. [BMS Creation Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7MuFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit) | “総出力” writes cut audio; III’s clipboard output is pasted into BMSE. [ぷるれこ guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) |
| **BMHelper / Mid2BMS** | Read MIDI, separate/reorder notes, output MIDI; render a separated stem in the DAW; copy cutting positions; load them in Woslicer; export slices; copy keysound definitions and BMS sequence to editor. Mid2BMS automates per-track MIDI/render/rename work more than BMHelper. [BMHelper](https://excln.github.io/bmhelper.html) · [Atwiki](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/12.html) · [FL/Mid2BMS guide](https://trap.jp/post/777/) | BMHelper itself does not cut audio; repeated DAW renders and external slicer remain. Definitions/sequence depend on exact starting number and file ordering. A documented BMHelper beta has a clipboard newline bug, and its clipboard data disappears when the app closes. [BMHelper](https://excln.github.io/bmhelper.html) · [Atwiki](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html) | No universal maximum; count is bounded downstream by format/editor/game. Mid2BMS source describes a dialog checking expected vs written WAV count. [FL/Mid2BMS guide](https://trap.jp/post/777/) | Renamed WAVs plus copied `#WAV` definitions and BMS sequence; optional batch WAV→OGG conversion. [FL/Mid2BMS guide](https://trap.jp/post/777/) |
| **PTSEQUENCER / DJMAX** | Publicly indexed reference says PTSEQUENCER’s DJMAX key-sound count was 1023 in DPC 2022, later reference text says DPC 2025 increased it to 2047. This is a format/tool limit, not a slicer workflow. [NamuWiki key sound](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C) · [DPC page](https://en.namu.wiki/w/DJMAX%20RESPECT%20V/DPC) | Capacity pressure; no public PTSEQUENCER slicer UX/shortcut specification was found. The reference also notes key sounds can be absent and Respect-era games have an option to play key sounds automatically regardless of gameplay. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C) | 1023 is the indexed DPC 2022 value; 2047 is the indexed DPC 2025 value. Do not hard-code one value without targeting the exact build. | No public export method found in this crawl. |
| **sound-slicer** | Read `.txt` timing plus a WAV, slice into numbered WAVs, generate BMx clipboard; keep source project files beside a `wav/` working folder. Rhythmic mode makes one slice/event; melodic mode groups same note/length/velocity and reuses slices. [README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) | Rhythmic mode can create 1000 slices for 1000 MIDI notes; melodic mode requires a second rendered MIDI/WAV pass. Both modes explicitly do not support BPM changes. It is a 2011 batch/script workflow. [README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) | No max; one-event-per-note in rhythmic mode; no BPM-change support. [README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) | Numbered WAVs plus generated BMx clipboard. [README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) |

## 2. Problem inventory

### Timeline / timing

| Severity | Evidence-backed problem | Product implication |
|---|---|---|
| **P0** | A placement export can be invalid or silently lossy: Sayaslicer warns that zero-cross movement can affect iBMSC data, and malformed/unsupported saves may lose keysounds or change gamemode; its BMSE fallback rounds to 192nd. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) | Make quantization and representability explicit before export; show “will round N markers” and block/offer repair rather than silently placing wrong notes. |
| **P1** | Woslicer is BPM/grid-oriented, while sound-slicer explicitly cannot handle BPM changes; Sayaslicer calls better BPM-change support a planned feature. [Woslicer notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7MuFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit) · [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) · [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) | Dual ms + musical ruler, tempo-map-aware grid, and per-marker absolute-time preview. |
| **P1** | Woslicer guides describe the waveform as useful, but placement is separated from BMSE chart placement and requires clipboard/file handoff. [BMS Creation Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7uFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit) | Show chart preview and slice markers in one synchronized timeline. |
| **P1** | Woslicer III’s documented click/pop behavior is a real boundary-quality failure, not merely a preference: investigation found a reverse/reflect tail and a one-sample zero around the fold point. [Qiita](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/79db943d2e3447adee71) | Audition boundaries, display zero-cross candidates, and provide reversible fade/tail policy per slice. |

### Interface / workflow

| Severity | Evidence-backed problem | Product implication |
|---|---|---|
| **P0** | The established route requires copying BMHelper positions, loading them in Woslicer, setting BPM, exporting, defining WAVs in BMSE, then pasting sequence data; BMHelper warns its clipboard must remain open until paste. [ぷるれこ](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) · [Atwiki](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html) | Replace the ceremony with a single project and “Import to Studio”; preserve source markers internally. |
| **P1** | Multi-file management is order-sensitive: BMSE definition start number and Explorer sort/order must match; users are instructed to keep files sorted and select the correct starting row. [ぷるれこ](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) | Use stable slice IDs, manifest-based export, and automatic collision/missing-file checks. |
| **P1** | BMHelper’s stated purpose is only to assist before/after cutting; it depends on Woslicer II and BMSE. [BMHelper](https://excln.github.io/bmhelper.html) | A slicer inside the editor should own timing, audio preview, definitions, and note placement. |
| **P2** | Sayaslicer’s keyboard model is strong, but legacy Woslicer’s controls are not discoverable from modern chart context; docs expose many single-letter operations (`Z/C/V/B/T/M/P`, BPM keys, A/S). [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) · [BMS Creation Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7uFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit) | Keep fast keyboard paths, add visible shortcut hints and remapping. |

### Settings / audio policy

| Severity | Evidence-backed problem | Product implication |
|---|---|---|
| **P1** | Woslicer II previews do not work for 32-bit-float WAVs. [BMS Creation Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7uFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit) | Decode common PCM/float formats or give an explicit conversion warning. |
| **P1** | Tail treatment is a manual concern in the basic guide; BMHelper’s minimum interval is specifically used to separate reverb/dry material and may need changing for delay. [Woslicer guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) · [BMHelper](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html) | Per-slice end mode: hard, zero-cross, fade, or preserve tail; show audible preview. |
| **P1** | Sayaslicer exposes arbitrary snapping and zero-crossing but warns zero-crossing changes marker timing; its fallback is nearest-192nd BMSE data. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) | Separate “audio boundary adjustment” from “chart timing”; store both values. |
| **P2** | The requested Sensitivity 0.55, Normalize, Auto-advance Grid/Beat/Off, and per-slice overrides were not found in the fetched public sources. | Treat these as proposed DJMax Studio settings, not validated incumbent conventions. |

### Backend / scale / runtime

| Severity | Evidence-backed problem | Product implication |
|---|---|---|
| **P0** | Traditional workflows materialize many files and definitions; sound-slicer’s rhythmic mode can produce one per MIDI note, and BMS delivery guidance says WAVs are “ridiculously large” and recommends OGG conversion. [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) · [BMS checklist](https://wcko87.github.io/bms-checklist/) | Non-destructive `{sourceFile,startMs,endMs}` is a high-value architectural improvement; finalize only when target format requires it. |
| **P1** | Sayaslicer’s >2 GB issue documents lag/unusable behavior from sample-count overflow; it was later fixed, but this is a useful regression case. [Issue #5](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/5) | Stream/decode waveform peaks, avoid whole-file audio buffers, and test long multichannel assets. |
| **P1** | Capacity is not uniform: BMS reference text says 1295 base-36 slots, BMSE later piloted base-62 to 3843; indexed DJMAX/PTSEQUENCER values are 1023 then 2047 depending on edition/year. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C) · [BMS Creation Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7MuFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit) | Mode switcher must validate against the selected target and provide reuse/merge suggestions before overflow. |
| **P1** | Some engines interrupt an already-playing sample when another sample arrives on the same track; the cited reference explains why reverb tails can be cut and why over-definition was used. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D음) | Target profiles should model overlap/polyphony and warn when a target will truncate tails. |
| **P2** | Legacy tools require WAV/OGG export and external conversion; no evidence in the fetched sources establishes a universal stereo/codec policy for all targets. [BMS checklist](https://wcko87.github.io/bms-checklist/) | Keep source codec independent from finalized export; validate channel count/sample rate only at finalize. |

## 3. What Sayaslicer did right vs Woslicer — keep these

* **Keep Woslicer’s speed and low-friction keyboard operation:** `Z`, `P`, arrow navigation, snap changes, and one-key export are concrete, repeatable actions. [BMS Creation Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7uFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit)
* **Keep Sayaslicer’s compatibility breadth:** BMSE clipboard, iBMSC clipboard, marker copy/paste, project save/load, MIDI marker import, Mid2BMS renamer import, and keysound-list export are all explicitly documented. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)
* **Keep explicit fallback behavior:** Sayaslicer tells users when iBMSC’s arbitrary resolution is unsafe and offers BMSE’s 192nd rounding path. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)
* **Keep non-destructive editing semantics where possible:** Sayaslicer’s project save and marker model, plus sound-slicer’s separation of original project files and `wav` output folder, support reopening work. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) · [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)
* **Do not copy Woslicer III’s boundary synthesis blindly:** the published investigation and guide both point to beginning clicks/pops; implement a tested zero-cross/fade algorithm instead. [Qiita](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/79db943d2e3447adee71) · [BMS Creation Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7uFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit)

## 4. Top 10 recommendations for DJMax Studio Slicer

1. **P0 — Make slices virtual by default.** Store `{sourceFile,startMs,endMs}` plus boundary policy and target ID; export WAV/OGG only on finalize. This removes the one-file-per-event burden evidenced by sound-slicer and BMS’s large-WAV guidance. [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) · [BMS checklist](https://wcko87.github.io/bms-checklist/)
2. **P0 — Ship “Import to Studio” as a transaction.** One action should create notes, a Slice Library, stable IDs, and a reversible link back to the source; it directly removes the BMHelper→Woslicer→BMSE handoff and clipboard lifetime failure. [ぷるれこ](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) · [Atwiki](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html)
3. **P0 — Build the proposed dual timeline.** Put waveform/ms ruler below and chart preview/bar-beat ruler above, with one synchronized playhead and zoom. Existing tools show waveform or generate clipboard, but the cited workflow keeps those views in separate apps. [BMS Creation Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7uFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit)
4. **P0 — Add target-aware capacity validation.** BMS base-36/base-62 and DJMAX/PTSEQUENCER counts differ; show count, reusable-slice count, overflow, and merge candidates for BMS/RESPECT/TECHNIKA modes. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D음)
5. **P1 — Separate chart time from audio boundary time.** A zero-cross move may reduce clicks but can corrupt arbitrary-resolution placement; store musical position and adjusted audio boundary separately, with a visible delta. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)
6. **P1 — Provide robust boundary tools.** Per-slice Zero-X on/off, fade length, preserve-tail/hard-cut, and audible A/B preview should be reversible. This responds to Woslicer III’s documented pop mechanism and BMHelper’s tail/delay concerns. [Qiita](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/79db943d2e3447adee71) · [BMHelper](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html)
7. **P1 — Make snapping tempo-map aware.** Offer 1/4 through 1/192, ms and sample views, absolute-time markers, and a clear “round on export” report. This addresses the documented 192nd fallback and weak BPM-change support. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) · [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)
8. **P1 — Use a manifest, never filename order.** Export a machine-readable mapping from slice ID to source range, note time, target key number, and finalized filename; validate missing/colliding files. This eliminates the documented Explorer sort/start-number fragility. [ぷるれこ](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)
9. **P1 — Design for long files and common audio formats.** Stream peak data, handle >2 GB assets, float PCM, stereo, and WAV/OGG without preview surprises; give actionable conversion diagnostics. [Sayaslicer issue #5](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/5) · [BMS Creation Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7uFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit)
10. **P2 — Preserve expert keyboard flow while improving discoverability.** Keep one-key marker/preview/navigation/export, add undo/redo, visible shortcut hints, and remapping. Sayaslicer and Woslicer demonstrate that keyboard-first operation is a strength worth carrying forward. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) · [BMS Creation Notes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ywUO5RxCP8jCM7uFGFAS5TIRK2gsyM3-rMgvPuMEcw/edit)

## Evidence gaps and non-claims

* The Sayaslicer public issue index showed six closed issues and no open issues at crawl time; therefore there are not ten current GitHub issues to summarize. [Issue index](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues?q=is%3Aissue)
* I found no public Woslicer II/III GitHub issue list, no authoritative PTSEQUENCER export manual, and no sufficiently specific YouTube comment corpus in the fetched results. I therefore do not attribute unverified complaints such as “silent double-placement,” “Sensitivity 0.55,” or a specific stereo/codec maximum to those tools.
* The cited Korean reference reports values by edition/year; “1023,” “2047,” and “1295/3843” must be treated as target-profile facts to verify against the exact DJMax Studio import/export implementation, not as one universal limit. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/키음)
